items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: I couldn’t say that I would stand up and be able to sing with Ornette Coleman, you know, I respect him

ctx.x: Well, as I said before, I’m not a technical musician as far as the written note is concerned. But what I have aspired to do, now that I’m being accepted in that gender as a jazz singer in some places, is to first of all as a vocalist, pay attention to what comes out of your mouth, what you are saying, the written word. You know as I say, technically, a lot of people who can read music can just pick up a lead sheet and sing the song. But your job is to make that song apply to someone. Try to be as true to the…

played piano. They were musicians. I couldn’t do that. So I had to pay attention to the word and the melody. And I find that to be a source of being able to handle the song. To me if I pay attention to what’s coming out at this point I just attempt to make a person listen to what I’m saying. To make it believable, you know. To have someone come up and say, “You know I’ve heard that song done a lot of times but when you sang it I really felt it,” you know. I think that is the payback for that. A lot of times I…
